verdict.reasoning: Both give a clear kill-for-now call with named conditions and stop rules, but Document 1's decision is more genuinely open and falsifiable: it pre-registers a specific probe (opt-in rate, exact baseline, n≈30, 4-week window, statistical + practical thresholds) that could concretely fail or pass, plus separate capacity/support guardrails. Document 2's 'success conditions' and signals (turnout, comprehension delta, confusion pulse) are reasonable but read more like a future execution plan for if/when the feature is built, and its verdict leans on an assumption (course/exam-date matching = homogeneous groups) asserted rather than tested, weakening the 'condition specific enough to turn out false' criterion.

Both reach the same 'competes, don't build now' call and identify similar risks (shared-ignorance ceiling, unvalidated one-pager falsifier), but Document 1's signals (match acceptance, comprehension delta) are post-launch metrics with no concrete pre-registered thresholds or timeline, making its stop condition vague ('low' or 'flat-to-negative'). Document 2 pre-registers a specific, cheap, falsifiable test (opt-in rate ≥20% vs 5% baseline, exact binomial test, n≈30, 4-week window) with explicit numeric stop/proceed rules and capacity guardrails, satisfying the rubric's demand for a specific observable signal and explicit stop condition far more rigorously.
